question: For the patient with an abnormal alkaliphophatase level, how many of them are admitted to the hospital?
evidence: abnormal alkaliphophatase level refers to ALP > = 300; admitted to the hospital refers to Admission = '+';
clarification: Count each distinct ID only once.
gold: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.ALP >= 300 AND T1.Admission = '+'
gold0: SELECT COUNT(T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.ALP >= 300 AND T1.Admission = '+'

c.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT P.ID) FROM Patient P INNER JOIN Laboratory L ON P.ID = L.ID WHERE L.ALP >= 300 AND P.Admission = '+'

d.request: For the patients with an abnormal alkaline phosphatase level (ALP >= 300), how many of them were admitted to the hospital (Admission = '+'), counting each distinct ID only once?
d.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT P.ID) FROM Patient AS P INNER JOIN Laboratory AS L ON P.ID = L.ID WHERE L.ALP >= 300 AND P.Admission = '+'

b.request: How many distinct patients with an ALP of at least 300 in any Laboratory record have Admission = '+' in the Patient table, counting each distinct ID only once?
b.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE l.ALP >= 300 AND p.Admission = '+'
